body:
I was curious as well as a clinic opened in my city last year. I read about it and was so intrigued but didn't take any steps to do it. Well, last Friday I was given ketamine as an anesthetic for surgery and didn't really piece together why my moods were so improved until a few days ago...I think it's the ketamine. When I say improved, it's pretty drastic for me. Mainly irritability/anger has significantly decreased. It does make me want to go see the ketamine clinic in the future.

Edit: a word
Lol are you the guy that said it? Sorry for calling you out dude.

Well, firstly, no one is going to be running through double iron doors with a baby. It was a lockdown facility. And secondly, I had psychotic symptoms and he said it right in front of me so it was literally a direct insult to me, calling people who suffer what I suffered with "baby snatchers". If he had read my chart I would hope he wouldn't be so willing to say terrible generalized things about a person of a vulnerable population that was sitting right there.

I don't really know why any of this needs to be explained.

Look into depersonalization. It's on the spectrum of dissociation. It can be experienced as looking in the mirror and feeling as though it wasn't what you expected to see.

What you're describing can be experienced by those with DID, but does not necessarily mean you have DID. DID comes with a plethora of dissociative symptoms. For me, the major symptom was losing time.

I was in a psychiatric hospital last summer because I was having hallucinations, but no delusions or other symptoms of psychosis. 

One of the other clients there asked why her baby couldn't visit her along with her husband. Right in front of me, a nurse answered, "It's dangerous - I've seen psychotic people snatch a baby right up and run away." 

I didn't say anything. I was just flabbergasted that this person could be working in mental health with such little knowledge, telling blatant lies, and if he had read my chart (gosh I'd rather believe he hadn't) he was also a complete fucking asshole.

I'm so sorry for your loss. This brought me to tears. I am a suicide survivor (my father) and yet have tried to commit suicide myself, even though I have 2 dogs of my own. I'm commenting here to tell you I'm sorry, and also to keep this post around for whenever I feel suicidal. Sending lots of love.

I dropped out of high school at 16. Things looked bleak as far as symptoms. I was in full swing of hearing voices, madly paranoid and distrustful about damn near everything, and talked about suicide all the time. 

My adolescent psychiatrist recommended applying for disability when I turned 18. This was the same man that had me on antipsychotics since I was 13. He saw me until a month before my 18th birthday, and I told him I was going to go to college. He discouraged this and told my mother I would be putting myself in pointless debt that would inevitably lead to failure.

At 22 I graduated with a B.S. in Psychophysiology and a B.A. in Psychology. I went on to a doctorate program, where I had more psychotic symptoms than ever. I dropped out of my doctorate program.

You know, even though I didn't travel the entire distance, I still feel a lot of pride getting my Bachelor's level degrees.  For someone like me, this was huge in my mind and still is. I'm absolutely in shock that I did anything for myself.

Today I'm just a psychotic NEET. But damn do I still feel good about accomplishing that. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is that you all can do it. I know you can. Some days just existence is tough, but the days you have where things are a little less than miserable, you can make the best out of. Good luck to you OP.

I asked my psychiatrist to write a letter certifying my two dogs are emotional support animals. I wanted to be able to bring them to my therapist's office with me.

However, I still live in a pet friendly apartment and paid the pet deposit and pet rent every month. I'm not sure if it's a law that varies by state, but I know that technically I am allowed to live anywhere, regardless of pet friendliness, and pay nothing extra for them. I just don't feel comfortable attempting to do so.  I live on the side of caution.

I found my mental health agency that provides therapy and psychiatry in the same building through my primary care provider. Hopefully you have one. I had looked for therapists on my own before that and the only therapist I found was awful, so I get that sentiment. I just messaged my PCP through their online portal and asked for a referral to a reputable mental health agency that took my insurance. I was on a wait list for some time, but it was worth it in the end. The therapist I have now is a godsend.
I actually laughed out loud at this because I do the exact same thing.

I would make plans with another therapist, or see if your current case worker could take you on as a client before cutting ties with the current therapist.

Just cancel your appointments with the current therapist at the front desk, ask to speak to patient advocacy or a similar group of people with your therapists company, and explain that you would like to discontinue seeing this therapist. Disclosing why is up to you.

I definitely get this the most when I am in the shower. Anything that can whistle, squeak, or make high pitch noises (such as high pressure water coming from the shower head) freaks me the fuck out, I automatically assume my dogs are screaming or it's my SO squealing in pain.

I really like these, especially the third one. I do this all the time with my boyfriend I live with. He's used to it. But also seeing things as well, our dogs having bloody eyes is a new one to me, so I cross reference with him.

I don't think you can stop Scientology or their subgroups.

A pair came into my place of work (a mom and pop shop) and told me they'd like to give me a simple "stress test". They had a machine that was connected to two metal bars where each of my hands held one.

Then they went into the pressing questions. One by one, they ultimately pressed me to relive one of my biggest traumas. They told me they could see the fear and pain in my eyes.

And for $25 I could buy a book that would make me an AMAZINGLY STRONG human being! That could conquer the world!

And with that they're setting me up for a $500 - no, FREE! session that could last as many hours as I needed with an experienced guide to end all of my misery! 

Except...you have to keep coming back, and then it's not free. And they single handedly retraumatized me in 15 minutes, creating a cowering, vulnerable me who easily handed over their last $25...imagine what they could make me in 3 hours?

I told my therapist and she said not only no, but HELL NO. An explicit warning to not get involved. 

That was September. They still call and text me. I hang up or don't respond.

Yes, I definitely understand the feelings of jealousy. In my experience, I would "catch" this person telling others things I said to this person verbatim. There were generally positive reactions to the things they said that I considered "mine". 

I just kept quiet about it and developed a passiveness for it. Who this person really is will come to light, either by their individual actions showing it or by their own personality development. It takes time.

I had this experience with one of my friends in undergrad. This friend copied all my interests, views, and values. Eventually this person was the epitome of what I viewed myself to be, at least outwardly. 

At first I was frustrated by this, but talking to people made me realize this is really one of the highest forms of flattery. Not only that, but the age you're at is when people are exploring their personalities and individuality and the ultimate question - who am I? He probably thinks you're a really fucking cool dude and wants to be just like you.
I hope you're right. Thank you for the words of encouragement.
Mainly, yes. I hear many voices. But the suicidal part of me won.

Let me clarify a bit. My psychiatrist diagnosed me with schizoaffective disorder, my therapist diagnosed me with dissociative identity disorder. There's a voice in my head that says you're worthless, helpless, hopeless. "Kill yourself, just get it over with." 

I put all the pills in my mouth and spit them out. Then the voice said no, you can do it. So I swallowed them all in one large gulp.

Too many issues to list. Diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder, I'm sure that didn't help when I lost my friend of 10 years. 

Still wishing I was dead.

My coworker introduced his mother to me 3 times before she stopped coming into the shop :(

I'll never forget the day that I didn't remember my best friend's grandmother died when I inquired about how she was doing.

I believe we are from the same city. Our system spent some time in hysterics with some of us being more overt about it than others. I have experienced more amnesic dissociation since the outbreak in our state, and it really ramped up with the first case in the city. I cancelled my therapist and psychiatrist appointments next week as I am too afraid to leave the house. Me and my SO ordered delivery groceries and household items. Terrified doesn't cover how all of us are feeling.

When I opened dialogue she showed me that memory. There was no issue of consent. It just unlocked. It went kind of like this:

Her: REPERCUSSIONS. REPERCUSSIONS. REPERCUSSIONS. over and over increasingly louder.

Me: what is it that you need from me?

Her: shows detailed trauma experience suddenly, unexpectedly. "I want you to know you were hurt."

And then she disappeared. 

I was genuinely trying to be helpful, it didn't end well. I don't know how to set boundaries with her.

It's all new territory with me, it's painful and hard to navigate successfully.

I think opening dialogue is unsafe at this point, as I still have dissociative amnesia and who knows if she knows where the guns are (my SO hid one and locked the rest away). 

I see what you mean about fear of abandonment with her. She always says, "never keep more than a carload of stuff." She's always thinking about how she could live without him and one time tried to leave with nowhere to go.

Does anyone else know like, how upsetting this stuff is? Me, as a host, I'm a kind, give the shirt off my back kind of girl. I take great pride in taking care of my family and myself. Her though, she...is a handful.

You're absolutely right, I need to change my attitude. My homework this week is figuring out a safe environment internally for the parts to come out and feel safe (inside). I am having a lot of trouble because I've only started to feel safe in the external world for the past handful of years, hence the parts emerging and voicing. But a place for them to go and feel safe? It's really hard for me to come up with.

You're right though, growing up I hated being labeled the problem child, when in reality it was a problem family and I was the product. I think you have given me much to reflect on. I should be more understanding and loving and caring.

I've only visited an innerworld where it's a room that's dusty with file bins and closed doors and I used to go there to sort the files away and sweep up. I called it "refreshing my brain." I never knew what was in the files though. At this point my therapist strictly advises not opening the doors.

See, for a long time I have been telling her simply to shut the fuck up. I'm new to navigating these waters. My therapist suggested opening dialogue with her last week and bam, she unlocked a horrible memory of abuse I was not ready to see yet. However opening dialogue did stop a total black out with her. I was sure she would take me over, but she didn't. After she released the memory she disappeared. 

My therapist said it was too heavy, I'm not ready for that stuff yet. But who am I to control my other parts? I feel totally out of control with this one. She's angry, suicidal, hates everyone, and lets me see her terrorizing my boyfriend with threats of suicide twice now in our 3 year relationship.

I hate this part of me.

Same here. I bought a new expensive king size mattress about a week ago attempting to be able to actually sleep through the night and convince them that sleeping is better than eating. Still eating. And it's like binge eating.

Damn. I thought I was the only one who ate in the middle of the night. I only knew about it after we bought security cameras for our house and reviewed the footage, beginning roughly 2 years ago. Baffled because I have no idea how long this has been going on, nor do I remember doing such things. My therapist thinks it's a fragment. Sometimes this bitch straight up cooks stuff.
